name: nav-buttons-animate
description: Reload's click nudges its glyph through the lab's reloadspin (sidebar-nav-row.css, ported from swipe-lab.html:68-69). A DOM class toggle proves the wiring but not the paint, so this reads it as pixels: a capture mid-animation must differ from rest (the spin is actually running), and a capture after animationend must match rest again (the class came back off, so a build that left the glyph stuck mid-turn is caught too). cgevent click/capture coordinates are SCREEN-absolute, not window-local: every Atrium window opens at pos=0,30 (move_window's own comment in vm-scenario.sh), so a point derived from CSS math alone needs +30 added to y before it reaches the button. The pointer is walked off the row after the click too, so the sticky :hover tint left behind by a real OS click cannot be mistaken for a stuck animation in the settled capture.

actions.note: first paint, and the nav row announces itself
the reload glyph at rest, before the click

reload's centre in SCREEN coordinates: x = 260 - kNavGroupRightInset(10) - half a 22px button(11) = 239, unshifted since the window's own x is 0. y = window pos.y(30) + .sbnav's top inset(9) + half the button height(11) = 50 - a sibling scenario's y=20 was window-local only and landed in the menu bar. Confirmed against the run's own frame: the reload glyph's painted pixels sit at screen x 234-243, y 44-54. A real OS click, so it clears AtriumClientView::NonClientHitTest before the DOM ever sees it.
well inside reloadspin's .45s (sidebar-nav-row.css) - the glyph is rotated partway through the turn, not yet back at rest
off the row and onto the page, so the pointer cgevent left parked over reload cannot keep .sbnav .nb:hover's background lit through the settled capture below
the spin finishes and animationend clears the class (sidebar-nav-row.js installReplayableAnimation), and the hover fade (.12s) clears behind the moved pointer
the glyph back at rest, the same as before the click

assertions.desc: THE MEASUREMENT: the glyph region changed mid-spin - the click actually started an animation, not just a state flip
the glyph settles back to its resting paint once animationend clears the class, rather than sticking mid-turn
the click also reached the reload message, not just the glyph
